newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica needs affirmative action - Nail head.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica needs affirmative action - Nail head.

text.p: Nthato Motlana, executive chairman of New Africa Investments Ltd, said on Thursday affirmative action should be part of a strategy to educate blacks to occupy higher positions in business.

"Affirmative action must not mean isolated response by big business to put black faces on the executive's management team. It needs to be part of a coherent social strategy in which education, training and mentorship play their part," Motlana told foreign correspondents.
He said if South Africa was to sustain stability, blacks should be allowed a share of the economy. Black economic empowerment would lead to the gradual easing of poverty along racial lines.
"Black economic empowerment means if not the ascendance of blacks in the economy then a preponderance of blacks that would slowly acquire wealth...(and) affluence will become multi-racial," he said.

Motlana said the recently completed deal by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd to sell the bulk of its 47.4 stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd to a consortium of black businesses, including Nail, indicated a paradigm shift in white business thinking.
"The Johnnic deal has shown a fundamental desire on the part of white business to empower blacks by directing assets directly into black hands," he said.
White business needed to show a willingness to transfer economic power to black people, otherwise government could be forced to intervene.
"There has to be a willingness to facilitate the shift of power...through white interest to blacks.

"If there is not such kind of willingness then I really doubt that black control of the economy can be reached without far-reaching government intervention and that will be highly undesirable," he said.
The consortium was looking at ways to add value to Johnnic through changing the pyramid structure of control, he said.

"I don't' think it (Johnnic) will continue in the kind of structure that it is. I believe some of the companies will be sold off for instance or consolidated...and come up with a structure that is cohesive and controllable."
He said days when Afrikaners used to say every black person should have a boss were over.

"If this country is going to have stability the idea that whites can control the likes of Johnnic and Anglo American are over...We demand a fair share of the cake of (the) economy and we want control," he said.
